Subject: MAP: POC benchmarks & technical next steps (post-call recap)

Hi Sofia — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed MAP milestones focused on the technical validation we discussed. I tried to keep milestones time‑boxed and with clear owners so we can get to a decision by the target close date.

High level goal: complete a short POC and benchmark run that validates latency, token cost, and QA/pass metrics on your clinical note retrieval workload. Target close date: 2026-11-20 (proposal).

Proposed MAP milestones (owners & due dates):
1) Baseline benchmark run (owner: Ben) — target window Oct 18–22
   - Success criteria: p95 inference latency <= 180 ms for 512-token requests (measured on hosted instance); 99th percentile <= 350 ms (see Ben's note below).
   - Cost target: average inference cost <= $0.06 per 1k tokens for the hosted candidate model with caching enabled.
   - Deliverable: bench report (latency percentiles, token-level cost, memory/KV hit rate).

2) Security & compliance evidence (owner: Sofia) — due Oct 20
   - Deliverable: redacted SOC2 report + data handling checklist so we can confirm mapping to Redwood Private options.

3) Integration POC + 48h stress run (owner: Connor) — target window Oct 25–Nov 5
   - Scope: run real prompts from your sample set (attached) against the shortlisted models on Redwood Dedicated with KV caching and batching enabled.
   - Success criteria: model shortlist accuracy (precision@K on labeled set) meets your acceptance thresholds (you flagged precision >= 0.88), and sustained throughput at expected concurrency with <5% error rate.
   - Deliverable: POC run logs + integration checklist + replayable artifacts.

4) Readout & decision (owner: Marissa) — target: Nov 16–20
   - Deliverable: final readout deck and recommended production configuration (hosted vs dedicated, quantization profile, routing policy).

Dependencies (items we need from HealthGrid):
- Finalized sample prompt set (we got an initial CSV in the call — please confirm).
- Expected concurrency profile (peak concurrent sessions, typical session length).
- Account contact to sign Dedicated trial/credit paperwork if we need a reserved slot.

Attachments: initial-map-draft.pdf (MAP + milestone table), sample-prompt-set.csv (first 250 rows).

Next steps I suggest: confirm the milestones above and who will own the checklist items on your side (security contact + integration lead). If that looks good we will lock the windows and Ben will start the baseline bench next week.

Thanks — Marissa

Thanks Marissa — looks good. A couple of quick technical clarifications from the bench perspective so expectations are aligned:

- Latency targets: I recommend tightening the primary p95 goal to <= 150 ms for the hosted candidate on 512-token requests (with prefix/KV caching enabled). We should still report p99 and tail behavior; p99 <= 400 ms is a reasonable fallback target. The reason is tokenization and batching variance can hide tail latency impact at higher loads.

- Cost model: We will report both token-level cost and end-to-end per-request cost (includes caching hit-rate adjustments). For fairness across shortlisted models we'll normalize to the same prompt set and batching config.

- Model shortlist (initial candidates for the POC):
  * Mistral-Chat-8B (dense)
  * Llama-3-13B (8-bit quant)
  * Redwood-optimized-quant-7B (micro-quant profile)

I'll start the baseline bench on Oct 18 unless you push the window. Also: please confirm whether we should include a longer tail test (48h low-burst run) as part of the baseline or reserve for the POC integration run.

Ben
Sr Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Looping in operational notes from my side. We can provision a Dedicated trial pool for HealthGrid for the POC windows; a few items I need to lock that down:

- Dataset size and expected concurrency (Sofia — do you have estimated qps/concurrent users for the POC? Ben guessed up to 50 concurrent test sessions earlier).
- Any hard requirements on model statefulness or session affinity (KV cache per user vs global).

For the 48h stress run I recommend the following config (to be reproducible in the readout):
- Dedicated pool: 4x A100-equivalent GPUs, batching window 20ms, KV cache enabled (per-session TTL 30m).
- Logging: token-level cost traces + sampling of raw inputs (PII redaction will be applied per your guidance).

On quantization: we can run a quick 1-day conversion test for the Llama-3-13B 8Q profile and compare quality delta vs dense. If HealthGrid is sensitive to hallucinations on specific prompt classes we should include a small labeled validation set to compute precision/recall.

I'll block tentative infra 10/25–11/05 and move it earlier if Ben's baseline shows a preferred candidate.
